entry.content: National Procrastination Week falls within the first two weeks of March. Officially set for the first week, it usually occurs the second week due to procrastination. Supported by Procrastinators’ Club of America, the goal is to celebrate the act of procrastinating by leaving necessary tasks to be done later. You can, however, put this off until next week. entry.title: Dogwood Festival, 2nd Weekend in April
entry.content: Held Friday through Sunday in Atlanta, Georgia, the Dogwood Festival is the city’s oldest fine arts festival. Dogwood trees are in full bloom, and artists from around the country display their work. All art is welcome, from paintings to photographs and sculptures to jewelry. There’s also music and food to round out the celebrations. Created in 1936 to boost community spirit during the Great Depression and celebrate Atlanta’s native dogwood trees. entry.title: Neurodiversity Pride Day, June 16
entry.content: Neurodiversity Pride Day was created in 2018 by the Neurodiversity Foundation to recognize and embrace neurological differences. It’s a day organized by neurodivergent people, for neurodivergent people, and their allies. This is part of a broader Neurodiversity Pride Week, with events leading up to this day. “Neurodiversity” refers to the idea that differences in how people’s brains work are natural and valuable, not deficits.
